en: The Apadāna of the Elder Ukkāsatika Naḷamāli Chapter 3.3 I was once a wood-gatherer, a laborer for wages; While gathering firewood, I saw the Buddha. At that time, the Teacher of the World was seated Under a tree, surrounded by a host of monks. Having seen him, I took up a torch And offered it to the one with the ten powers. Because of that gift of a torch, I have been reborn in the world of the gods. For eighty-four thousand aeons I dwelt in the realm of the Thirty-Three. Thereafter, having passed away from there, I was reborn among human beings. In every birth I was born into a noble family, Possessing great wealth and abundant grain. I was always handsome and fair to behold, With a body adorned with the marks of excellence. For eighty-four thousand aeons I never experienced suffering. In my final existence, I attained the state of a monk, And I have realized the goal of my ascetic life. I have seen the Four Noble Truths, Which are profound and difficult to perceive. Through the power of that gift of a torch, I have attained the supreme fruit of Arhatship. Thus did the Elder Ukkāsatika speak his own ancient account.
“At that time, the Blessed One named Kosiya dwelt on Cittakūṭa;
the Buddha was a meditator, delighting in jhāna.”
The sage, delighting in solitude,
having plunged into the Himalayas,
was surrounded by a host of women.
I saw the Buddha Kosiya,
like the moon on a full-moon night;
having seized him, he coughed.
I was then surrounded by a retinue;
having stayed for seven nights and days,
I departed on the eighth.
Having paid homage with a clear mind to the Buddha, the self-arisen, the unconquered, who has emerged from his seclusion like a sheath of silk, [I speak].
I gave a single alms-meal,
O Best of Bipeds, Eldest in the World, Bull among Men; by that kamma—
I was reborn in the Tusita realm;
this is the fruit of giving a single alms-meal.
Day and night, indeed, [I remained there].
There is always light for me;
I pervade a hundred leagues all around with radiance.
In the fifty-fifth aeon,
I was a wheel-turning monarch,
a conqueror of the four quarters.
The lord of Jambumaṇḍa.
At that time, my city was prosperous, flourishing, and well-constructed.
Thirty yojanas in length and twenty in width was the city named Sobhana.
It was constructed by Vissakamma;
it resounded with ten kinds of sounds,
perfectly attuned to the rhythm of drums and cymbals.
In that city there was no reed, wood, or clay;
it was entirely made of gold.
It shines at all times.
It was surrounded by four walls,
three of which were made of jewels.
And in the middle, a row of palm trees was fashioned by Vissakamma;
[there were] ten thousand lotus ponds.
Covered with pink and blue lotuses,
overspread with white lilies,
and scented by various fragrances.
For ninety-four eons,
since I have maintained this lamp,
I do not recall ever being born in an unhappy state.
This is the fruit of being a torch-bearer:
the defilements have been incinerated by me... [and so forth].
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me... [and so forth].
This is the teaching of the Buddha:
the four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Ukkāsatika recited these verses.
This is the third *apadāna* of the elder Ukkāsatika.
